subject: Request: Executive Signoff — Orion Health ramp & downsell protections
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exec signoff on Orion Health ramp + downsell protections

Team —

Quick ask: Orion Health (pilot customer, legal/procurement looped) wants an on-paper ramp + early-exit safety net built into the SOW before they sign. The commercial asks are non-standard and need executive signoff:

Summary of customer request (from procurement call yesterday):
- 3-month ramp: committed spend schedule: Month 1 = $75k, Month 2 = $125k, Month 3 = $200k.
- After month 4 they want a 30-day opt-out to downsize commitment to a reduced floor of $60k/mo or to fully terminate with an early-termination credit.
- Requesting a 20% one-time introductory credit applied to month 1 and a 12% discount for the first 6 months as part of the ramp.
- Wants explicit language that, if they downsize during the first 12 months, the downside protection limits the customer's liability to the committed ramp months (i.e., no clawbacks beyond committed months).

Attached: current SOW draft (Orion_SOW_v3.pdf) and a draft ramp addendum (ramp_addendum_draft.docx) with suggested language.

Ask: Exec signoff on (a) whether we can approve the discount/credit mix, and (b) whether the proposed downsell/opt-out language is acceptable as-is or needs guardrails (finance/legal checks). If approved, I will send the addendum to procurement and request countersignature.

Why now: Procurement wants redline and commercial sign-off by Monday to meet their internal board review.

Appreciate fast takes — low-risk customer strategically (large potential ARR) but we need a clean approach to protect economics.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Attachment: Orion_SOW_v3.pdf (draft) ; ramp_addendum_draft.docx (draft)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec signoff on Orion Health ramp + downsell protections

Sergio — thanks for the summary and the drafts. A few legal clarifications before we approve commercially:

1) "Downsize" and "terminate" language needs to be precise. We should:
   - Define the "Downsell" as a one-time downward amendment to committed units with a minimum 60-day notice and a maximum of one permitted downsell in the first 12 months.
   - If they terminate early, the early-termination credit should be a defined pro-rata refund of prepaid committed amounts less a termination fee (we typically allow 10–25% depending on deal size).
2) We must avoid language that caps our future pricing increases or locks us in on discounts beyond the defined term.
3) Add a clause that any material change to usage that causes overages will be billed at standard rates and not be subject to the ramp discount.

I'll redline the addendum to reflect the above. From a legal risk perspective this is acceptable if finance is comfortable with the financial concessions.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec signoff on Orion Health ramp + downsell protections

Appreciate the details. High-level finance view and modeled impact:

- Baseline ARR if customer stays at committed ramp schedule: ~$2.45M ARR year 1 (annualized after ramp).
- The requested commercial gives: 20% one-time credit (~$15k impact in month 1) + 12% discount first 6 months (~$110k revenue concession over 6 months assuming full utilization).
- If we permit unrestricted downsell/termination right after month 3 without constraints, downside exposure could be material (we see worst case of ~$350k recognized revenue loss over the year).

Recommended guardrails to be comfortable:
1) Cap combined commercial concessions (credits + discounts) to no more than 18% of year 1 committed revenue.
2) Limit customer to a single permitted downsell in the first 12 months, with a minimum notice of 60 days, and an applied floor equal to 75% of the month 3 committed value unless they terminate (i.e., downsell floor $150k/mo). If they want a lower floor, it requires finance/exec approval.
3) Early-termination credit: pro-rata return of prepaid unused committed amounts less a 15% early-termination fee to cover onboarding and infra costs.
4) Require customer to sign the addendum and accept that any overages during ramp are billed at standard retail price (no retro discount).

If sales wants to proceed with a 15% net concession cap and the downsell floor at 60% of month 3, I can run final ARR impact and give a clean approval number.

—Rishi Malhotra
VP, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec signoff on Orion Health ramp + downsell protections

Team —

Thanks for the fast turn. My read: strategic account, good short-term ARR upside, and they are in a regulated vertical (healthcare) so pilots can move slowly. I'm comfortable with a limited concession set that we can operationalize. My recommendation:

- Approve up to 15% total net concession (credits + discounts).
- Approve the 3-month ramp schedule as submitted.
- Downsizing allowed once in first 12 months with 60-day notice, and the downsize floor must be 60% of month 3 spend ($120k minimum).
- Early termination allowed with pro-rata refund minus a 15% termination fee.
- Require procurement to sign the ramp addendum and for Legal to confirm the final redlines before countersignature.

If Marissa/execs are aligned I recommend we accept that package — keeps economics intact while removing a key barrier to signing. Sergio, please capture this in the addendum and request a countersign.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Exec signoff on Orion Health ramp + downsell protections

Sergio / team —

Executive decision: conditional approval granted with the following firm limits — these are non-negotiable from the leadership side:

1) Total commercial concessions (one-time credits + ongoing ramp discounts) must not exceed 15% of year 1 committed revenue.
2) Downsizing allowed a maximum of one time in first 12 months; must provide 60 days' notice. Downsize floor is 60% of month 3 committed spend ($120k minimum).
3) Early termination: pro-rata refund of prepaid committed amounts less a 15% termination fee.
4) Legal to finalize redline; customer countersign required before provisioning.

Sergio: get written acceptance from procurement on these terms (email + countersigned addendum). Once we have that, Legal can finalize and we can provision. If any element deviates materially from these constraints, bring back to me for re-approval.

Marissa Cole
GM, North America Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Orion Health Procurement <procure@orionhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Updated: Orion Health SOW & Ramp Addendum — final commercial terms for signature

Elena —

Great speaking with you yesterday. Thanks for the transparency around timelines. Per our internal review, Redwood is prepared to move forward with the following commercial package; this is the final offer pending your countersignature on the attached addendum:

- Ramp schedule (committed spend): M1 $75k, M2 $125k, M3 $200k.
- One-time introductory credit of $12k applied to month 1.
- 12% discount will apply to months 1–6, with total concessions capped at 15% of year 1 committed revenue.
- Downsizing is permitted once in the first 12 months with 60 days' notice; downsize floor is 60% of M3 ($120k).
- Early termination permitted with pro-rata refund of unused prepaid committed amounts less a 15% termination fee.
- Overages billed at standard published rates and are not retroactively discounted.

Attached: final redline of the SOW and the ramp addendum (Orion_SOW_Final_for_Signature.pdf). Please review with your procurement team; if acceptable, reply to this thread with written acceptance and return the signed addendum via DocuSign.

If you want to chat through any line items, happy to jump on a short call early next week to close.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
